description: Read the base case and recursive multiplication step of factorial in Scheme.

steps.description: Lines 1-4 bind `factorial` to `(lambda (n) ...)`. When `(= n 0)` is true on line 3, line 4 returns the base-case value `1`.
When `n` is non-zero, line 5 evaluates `(* n (factorial (- n 1)))`, multiplying `n` by the factorial of `(- n 1)`.
Notice how each recursive call passes `(- n 1)` on line 5, counting `n` down by `1` until it reaches `(= n 0)` on line 3.

steps.question: When `(factorial 5)` runs on line 7, what chain of multiplications is waiting when `(factorial 0)` reaches line 4, and what number does it return?

title: Recursive Factorial with define and lambda
